summary: Three Fairbanks police arrests made on Saturday, Nov. 7, became public records overnight: a felony assault with a weapon on O'Connor Road, a misdemeanor assault on South University Avenue, and a six-count arrest at Lakeview Terrace that includes two felony counts of theft of an access device. Court cases had already been opened behind the two assault arrests; no case has been filed behind the Lakeview Terrace arrest. No criminal case has been opened at the Fairbanks, Nenana, Healy or Delta Junction courthouses since Saturday afternoon, and Alaska State Troopers reported no incident in the Fairbanks area on Nov. 8. One hearing is set for Sunday, a continued arraignment at 1:30 p.m. The filing counts below are the Alaska Court System weekly charges report's own counts for its window of Nov. 1 to Nov. 7; that report was run at 9 p.m. on Nov. 7 and includes every case the courts opened inside the window. The statewide dispositions report has not been updated since Nov. 2, so no case closed in the Interior since then appears in any court document.

entries.title: Felony theft arrest: Julia Ann Pitka
body: Julia Ann Pitka, 38, was arrested on two counts of theft in the second degree of an access device — taking a credit card, debit card or similar device — which police record as felonies. The same arrest carries theft in the fourth degree of property worth less than $250, buying or selling an access device or identification, and two counts of violating conditions of release, all recorded by police as misdemeanors.
1100 block of Lakeview Terrace 1 Road, Fairbanks, Nov. 7 at 4:32 p.m.; Fairbanks Police. Police case 26003389.

No criminal case has been filed in court behind the arrest. A search of Alaska court records on the name returns no case filed on Nov. 7 or Nov. 8 at any court in the state, so the charge classifications above are the police department's own and not a court's.

entries.title: Felony assault arrest: Harlen Lee Captain
body: Harlen Lee Captain, 29, is charged with assault in the second degree — intentionally causing injury with a dangerous instrument — a Class B felony, punishable by up to 10 years. He is also charged with criminal mischief in the fifth degree, damaging property worth less than $250, a Class B misdemeanor. The court record lists both counts as domestic violence related and gives an offense date of Nov. 7 at Fairbanks.
According to the Fairbanks Police daily bulletin, he was arrested at the 1100 block of O'Connor Road, Fairbanks, on Nov. 7 at 2 a.m. Police case 26003394.
Case 4FA-26-02245CR. He was arraigned Nov. 7, counsel was appointed from the bench and the next event is set for Nov. 17.

sources.label: Alaska Court System weekly charges report

entries.title: Assault arrest: David Titus Peter
body: David Titus Peter, 37, is charged with assault in the fourth degree — placing another person in fear of imminent injury — a Class A misdemeanor. The court record lists the count as domestic violence related and gives an offense date of Nov. 7 at Fairbanks.
According to the Fairbanks Police daily bulletin, he was arrested at the 1700 block of South University Avenue, Fairbanks, on Nov. 7 at 4:30 a.m. Police case 26003395.
Case 4FA-26-02246CR. He was arraigned Nov. 7 before Judge Bahr; next event Dec. 24.

sources.label: Alaska Court System weekly charges report

entries.title: Arraignment set for Sunday: Elaina Deborah Carroll
body: Elaina Deborah Carroll is charged with assault in the fourth degree — recklessly causing injury — a Class A misdemeanor, recorded by the court as domestic violence related, with an offense date of Nov. 6 at Fairbanks.
Her arraignment on Nov. 7 was continued, and she is set to be arraigned at 1:30 p.m. on Nov. 8 in Courtroom 102 of the Fairbanks courthouse before the weekend and holiday judge.
Case 4FA-26-02244CR. A pre-trial conference is set for Jan. 7, 2027 and a trial week from Jan. 19, 2027.

entries.title: DUI charges confirmed at Delta Junction: Chad James De Long
body: Chad James De Long is charged with driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance, refusing to submit to a chemical test, and driving with a license canceled, revoked or suspended for a criminal offense. All three are Class A misdemeanors and all three are dated Oct. 31 at Delta Junction.
The case was filed at the Delta Junction courthouse on Nov. 6 and now appears in the state court system's weekly charges report for Nov. 1 to Nov. 7.
